_doc: T310 proposal (status: proposed; main approves it together with the SI1 key poses, d-04 section 1). Weapon socket convention for the player: how a weapon mesh is placed on DEF WeaponSocket_R / WeaponSocket_L. Axes are the socket bone's local axes (Blender, canonical_skeleton.json v1.1; head = fist centre). World vectors below are Blender world (front -Y, up +Z, character left +X), measured on PL_rig (pl_r04_ctrl.blend) by a scratch probe of T310.

convention.pivot: grip centre = socket head (the fist centre: the M_fist_r vertex centroid lies 0.2 mm from the WeaponSocket_R head at rest and at the ready pose)
convention.blade_axis: +Z (grip -> tip). At rest the socket +Z points world forward (the thumb side of the hanging relaxed fist); with the elbow flexed the fist's natural up becomes +Z, so an upright sword needs no socket offset
convention.guard_axis: Y (the socket's long axis, along the hand / forearm): the guard sits across the top of the fist over the knuckle-to-wrist line
convention.attach: Child Of constraint on the weapon object, target PL_rig, subtarget WeaponSocket_<side>, inverse matrix identity, object transform identity (object world = socket head matrix @ object local)
convention.mesh_space: a weapon mesh is authored in this socket space: origin at the grip centre, blade along +Z, guard along Y
convention.left: the same local convention on WeaponSocket_L (its +Z is also world forward at rest; its X is mirrored, which a mesh symmetric about X ignores)

WeaponSocket_R.note: Sword_Idle f1 (pl_a_Sword_Idle.blend, inspect/clips/Sword_Idle/SI1_measure.json): upper arm X -15 / Y 45 / Z 10, lower arm X 65, hand X 5 / Y 30; blade 12.6 deg outward from vertical

placeholder_sword.use: preview only (Blender sheets; Unity later); never in Player.fbx or the stage

unity.attach: identity local transform under WeaponSocket_<side> (Unity); the compensation is baked into the weapon FBX

export_compensation.applied_to: the socket-space weapon mesh before the FBX export (p34_weapon_preview.py), export with the player preset + bake_space_transform True, object_types MESH
export_compensation.derivation: K = Qu^-1 . C . Rb (Unity rest world rotation of WeaponSocket_<side> from unity/AvatarCheck/player_report.json rest; Blender rest_matrix from data/canonical_skeleton.json; C = export_preset axis_mapping blender_to_unity); a baked export maps v -> C . v, so P = C^-1 . K. Measured K_R = [[-1.0000001570266774, -6.53243094489367e-08, 2.8409721280629422e-08], [-3.598804872561403e-08, 1.0000000985032824, -2.0834098435167092e-08], [9.091850848527442e-09, 1.3690076797016892e-08, 0.9999998646804417]], K_L = [[-0.9999999619230974, 4.2291264775995604e-07, -1.2502750052055385e-08], [3.821396871089148e-07, 0.9999999869884124, -8.889442257471736e-08], [-7.861547313471203e-09, 7.23330738361394e-08, 1.0000000437523786]] (Unity bone-local = Blender bone-local with x negated); |P_R - P_L| = 4.88e-07 (one rotation for both sides); det 1.000000; snapped to the nearest signed permutation (residual 1.57e-07)
export_compensation.note: a bone frame mapped as a rotation (C . R . C^T) differs from the Unity bone rotation by Rx(90) on every bone; the axis mapping of the frame (C . R) differs only by the x flip K, which is what an identity child inherits
